title: So how is Fable?
author: Lucky_Pangolin_3760
selftext: Worth getting Claude and maxing out the weekly limit or not?

comments.author: ffxivthrowaway03
comments.body:
Ignore the reddit hype.  It's not some magic bullet thats 2000% better at development tasks.

You're not doing cybersecurity research, you don't need a Mythos class model that eats through your wallet in seconds. Whatever your current model is will be perfectly fine.

replies.author: Lucky_Pangolin_3760
replies.body: I just remember seeing someone making Minecraft with Fable which seemed pretty impressive

replies.author: ffxivthrowaway03
replies.body: You can do the same thing with Opus 4.8, with a hell of a lot less tokens.  Minecraft is not a complex game.  Voxel art is easy because it's literally just math - no hand-authored assets, and the rest of the game is just a basic physics engine and an algorithmically created grid of blocks.  Any modern LLM would absolutely excel at recreating minecraft with minimal effort.

replies.author: tomqmasters
replies.body: There are dozens of examples online how to make minecraft in every language and every game engine/framework basically.  Gpt3.5 probably could have come close with how much training data there is for that particular problem.

replies.author: BertJohn
replies.body:
ChatGPT like over 2 years ago could have remade minecraft with incredible accuracy. Its a commonly used theme in LLM's to the point that we've exceeded what minecrafts max potential could be i feel, Like rendering 8km render distance video. 

  
You can even push it harder with texture maps and implement really fast water simulation.

comments.author: r3v3rs3r
comments.body: I would say the only real difference that I have noticed is if you ask it to complete several tasks at a time in one prompt, it will go as far as it can to complete them all, instead of completing one task and then asking to go onto the next task, which is pretty nice, but ultimately not worth the amount of token burn.

replies.author: Kindly_Life_947
replies.body: you can mitigate some of the issues by asking fable to delegate simple work to sonnet when fable is not needed

replies.author: r3v3rs3r
replies.body: Pretty cool, I wasn't aware, thanks!

comments.author: SillyVermicelli7169
comments.body:
It does great at planning.

I tested planning with Sonnet and Opus, then had Fable review the plans and it found several factual errors.

Now I'm creating the plan with Fable and having Sonnet or Opus execute, e.g. adding 3rd party services, analytics events, etc.

comments.author: forrestwear
comments.body:
fable is good if you have $ to blow and you already have an idea on what you want to make. 

fable will not shorten the gap between a bad game, and a good game. that is 100% up to the user. 

it's worth getting claude for opus alone. long as you're not trying to build games in one shot prompts, 20 dollars a month is plenty. long as you get the most out of your free resources (free chat gpt, free deepseek flash) and plan your sessions, opus is more than enough. 

fable will write better code and run into less bugs. it will find solutions that opus can't. but game dev is not absolute. it all depends on the user.

replies.author: Turbulent-Armadillo9
replies.body: I actually use opus as my big boy and do other stuff with cheaper models. I dunno man maybe it’s just my project is simple enough but I actually never feel like I need more and better ai 🤗

comments.author: tomqmasters
comments.body: It's a noticeable improvement.  Idk if I can tell how much better the model itself is, but they implemented guiderails that do a good job keeping it on track for larger problems.  For $20 a month I don't think it's hard to justify.

comments.author: wizzard_rick
comments.body:
Overall, I liked it. I ran it in the following mode: “Fable handles the architecture and requirements specification, a subagent on Opus handles the task, and Fable reviews it.” In a full day, I used up about 20% of my weekly limits.

The tasks I had it perform were done much better than they had been done previously by Opus.

I also use Codex all the time, which I really like, but Fable is pretty good.

comments.author: blanktarget
comments.body: Been good. It seems to take the time to play test and make sure its change worked and also much better at shaders imo.
